To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the number of active cells, their spike timing and the number and timing of spikes in individual neurons are not significantly different during normal and blocked gill withdrawals; (2) the summed spike activity and the number of active ganglion cells during normal and blocked withdrawals are not significantly different; and (3) trial‐to‐trail differences in summed spike activity and number of active cells during blocked withdrawals do not differ significantly from differences between two normal trials.
